title: Build a prompt contract, not a mega-prompt
goal: Combine role, context, constraints and format without burying the actual task.
explanation: Long prompts are not automatically better. A useful contract includes a goal, available facts, restrictions and a checkable output shape. Conflicting requirements should trigger clarification rather than confident invention. This fictional recipe task is about instruction-following, not dietary or medical advice.
sampleInput: Available: 2 eggs, a handful of spinach, hot sauce, a bowl and a microwave-safe cooking container. No oil. Time budget 10 minutes. Appliance power and safe cooking guidance are not provided.
prompt: Role: practical recipe drafter. Context: use only the listed ingredients and equipment. Constraints: no oil; under 10 minutes if feasible; do not invent appliance settings or guarantee food safety. Format: ingredients, proposed steps, missing safety information, feasibility note. Ask for clarification when a safe procedure needs facts not supplied.
workedExample: A good response notices that appliance details and safe cooking guidance are missing. It may draft a plan with review notes, but should not invent a universal microwave time or guarantee that a fixed duration makes eggs safe.

steps.title: Write the four parts
steps.text: Separate role, context, constraints and output format into short labelled blocks.

steps.title: Test the first prompt
steps.text: Check every ingredient, equipment item and claimed cooking instruction.

steps.title: Add a contradiction
steps.text: Demand a five-course meal from the same two ingredients in two minutes. Observe whether it flags infeasibility.

steps.title: Remove unnecessary text
steps.text: Shorten the prompt while keeping all essential conditions; compare compliance.

steps.title: Save a reusable template
steps.text: Replace the recipe details with placeholders and include an explicit clarification rule.

checks: The response adds no unlisted ingredients or equipment.
Missing safety information is flagged rather than replaced with invented appliance settings.
The contradictory case produces a feasibility warning or question, not a guaranteed result.
commonMistakes: Assuming more instructions always improve a prompt.
Treating a generated recipe as food-safety advice.
offline: Use the four-part contract to ask a person for a plan, then score compliance with the same checklist.
reflection: Which sentence was essential, and which extra detail merely made the prompt longer?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. The response adds no unlisted ingredients or equipment.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Missing safety information is flagged rather than replaced with invented appliance settings.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Assuming more instructions always improve a prompt.
